clue.text: Bard's close by, touring one Scottish island?

definitions.note: Shakespeare, the Bard, uses this phrase to mean very near at hand

parts.note: someone touring a place is at it, visiting, so the word gives the little preposition
the indefinite article stands for one
an inch is a small island in Scottish place-names, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: Shakespeare comes near, on a visit to some Hebridean isle.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH (from Gaelic innis) is a Scottish word for a small island. The question mark flags that 'touring' is loosely clued as AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Shakespearean idiom for 'very near', used in Henry VI, so it fits the Bard's way of saying nearby.

clue.text: See 21
Raised counter cut jaw

definitions.note: a verb here: to talk at length

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served
a bit is a piece cut off something

explanation.surface: A counter has been lifted up and someone's jaw got cut in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaw' looks like the body part, but it is the slang verb for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering endlessly, just as to jaw is to talk tediously.

clue.text: Oil well running dry primes hooter

indicators.note: the oil well is set running, its letters set in motion into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays off alcohol

explanation.surface: A gushing oil well that runs dry gets things primed with a loud hooter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primes' simply joins the wordplay to the definition. 'Hooter' looks like a siren or a nose, but here it is a bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: This small European owl is a hooting bird, and a hooter is a playful name for any owl.

clue.text: Venerated international section

parts.note: a conic, or conic section, is a curve made by slicing a cone

explanation.surface: An international section of something is held in great reverence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section' sounds like a part of a document, but it is the geometry term.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iconic is revered as a symbol, treated with near-religious veneration like an icon.

clue.text: Whether opinion is wrong or ultimately misplaced, this book's 100 years old

indicators.note: the words are got wrong, jumbled into a different order
a letter that has been misplaced has gone missing from the fodder

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word or

parts.note: the word whose last letter goes missing

explanation.surface: Whatever anyone thinks, this book reached its centenary.
explanation.walkthrough: The book was published in October 1926, so the puzzle marks its hundredth anniversary; the rest of the clue states that fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's first collection of Pooh stories is the book the clue points to, a centenarian children's classic.

clue.text: See 25
Undergoing measured withdrawal remedy worries glum type

indicators.note: letters are withdrawn at measured, regular intervals, so every other one is dropped

parts.note: taken as written; its even-placed letters survive

explanation.surface: A cure for anxiety is being phased out gradually, like a drug being tapered.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of the phrase gives the gloomy donkey from the Pooh stories.
explanation.definitionFit: The donkey in Milne's stories is famously pessimistic, so his name stands for any gloomy, downbeat person.

clue.text: Forgoing old official meeting place

indicators.note: the official is forgoing, doing without, one letter

parts.note: a coroner is an official who investigates sudden deaths

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned official has given up a venue for meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner is where two streets or walls meet, a literal meeting place of lines or roads.

clue.text: Working round, we sons will get by

definitions.text: Working round, we sons will get by

indicators.note: the letters are worked round, turned about into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Our boys will get by doing a delivery round.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: lads earning a living on a paper round.
explanation.definitionFit: Paperboys deliver newspapers on a round, which is how such sons scrape a little money together.

clue.text: Gives birth with staff lending a hand

parts.note: domestic staff are often called the help
in bridge the four hands are named North, East, South and West

explanation.surface: A woman delivers her baby with the staff lending assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: S is South, one of the four hands in a game of bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as dogs whelp when they produce young, a verb for giving birth to pups.

clue.text: The AA responsible for 6 acceleration cuts in motorway lane

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 written as the letter I

indicators.note: the acceleration cuts out, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: taken as written, before its letter for acceleration is cut
a is the symbol for acceleration in physics

explanation.surface: The Automobile Association warns that speeding up cuts in on a motorway lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The AA' poses as the British motoring organisation, but it is the author's initials, A. A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Alexander wrote the Pooh books, so his initials make him the A. A. behind the 6-down classic.

clue.text: Cleric opens flatpack guide

indicators.note: the cleric sits inside, opening up the other word

parts.note: flatpack furniture is assembled at home, a classic DIY job
a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar opens up a flatpack instruction leaflet.
explanation.definitionFit: A directory is a reference listing that guides users to names, addresses or files.

clue.text: Bouncer "the one starting trouble": Archer's latest to be dropped

indicators.note: a letter to be dropped is left out of the word

parts.note: a trigger is what sets trouble off

indicators.note: the latest of a word is its final letter

parts.note: Archer, whose last letter goes; the 's only marks possession

explanation.surface: A nightclub bouncer is blamed for the fight, and an archer's latest shot misses.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIGGER without the R at the end of Archer leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tigger, the tiger in Winnie-the-Pooh, is famous for bouncing about on his tail.

clue.text: Man acting she does without — she's checked by me

indicators.note: she does without the acting letter, losing it

parts.note: a char is a woman who does housework
A. is the abbreviation for acting in a title such as acting captain
if she is checked by me, I stop her

explanation.surface: A man performs while a woman goes without; then she is restrained by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: A char, or charwoman, is a British cleaning woman, one who 'does' for a household. Christopher Robin is the boy in the Pooh books.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a male given name, so it is an example of a man, apt for the boy who owns Pooh.

clue.text: Observer's on top of it of course, and others not present know about it

indicators.note: the other letters go about it, the word for of course

parts.note: et al. is the Latin abbreviation for and others
yes is an emphatic of course

indicators.note: know without the present leaves only its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, before the part meaning present is removed
now means at present

explanation.surface: Someone well informed is on top of things, and absent colleagues already know about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is literal: a crab's or snail's eye sits on top of this organ.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyestalk is the movable stalk carrying an eye at its tip, so the observing eye is perched on top of it.

clue.text: Vulgar guy stabs Mafia boss

indicators.note: the guy stabs into the boss, going inside him

parts.note: a capo heads a Mafia crime family
he stands for any male

explanation.surface: A man knifes a mob leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is slang for cheap and tacky, close to vulgar in the sense of tasteless or low-grade.

clue.text: 6 originally heading for retirement perhaps putting billion aside

indicators.note: putting the billion to one side removes it from the word
set aside means taken out of the word and left to one side

parts.note: bedward means heading towards bed, retiring for the night

explanation.surface: Someone heading for retirement sets a billion aside.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Bear was Pooh's name in his first appearances, so the 6-down hero was originally called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Milne first introduced the bear as Edward Bear, the toy's original name before he became Pooh.

clue.text: Huge step, Busted recruiting leader for original band

indicators.note: the jumbled letters recruit, taking in, one more
the words are busted, broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

indicators.note: the leader for a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A big move: the pop group Busted takes on the original band's frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: Busted is a British pop band, which makes it look like a name, but here it signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pogues were a London Irish folk-punk group, so the name is an example of a band.

clue.text: Squealer fractured leg digging hole

indicators.note: the leg is digging into the hole, ending up inside it

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground

indicators.note: the leg is fractured, its letters broken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An informer broke a leg falling into a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squealer' suggests a police informer; it is a young pig, and the small pig of the Pooh books.
explanation.definitionFit: A piglet is a young pig, an animal known for squealing, hence a squealer.

clue.text: Arctophilia secreted in undergarment?

definitions.meaning: Greek arktos means bear: the word names the hobby of collecting cuddly toy ursine figures
the one-piece women's undergarment shares its name with the cuddly toy, so the collectibles are hidden in it

explanation.surface: A hobbyist's cuddly passion is hidden away in someone's lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the joke: a teddy is a woman's all-in-one undergarment, so the collector's objects are tucked into one.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctophiles collect stuffed toy bears, the very objects named by the two-word answer.

clue.text: Examining unfledged songbird

indicators.note: an unfledged chick lacks its feathers, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: probing means examining closely

explanation.surface: Inspecting a young bird that has not yet grown its feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Robin also links it to the Pooh theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a small European songbird with a red breast, an example of a singing bird.

clue.text: Furniture-maker catching on keeps joke about jumper

indicators.note: turned about, the whole assembly is read backwards
the wood catches the next part, holding it inside

parts.note: oak is a timber that furniture is made from

indicators.note: the short word keeps the joke inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a rag is a prank or joke, as in student rag week

explanation.surface: A cabinetmaker catches on and keeps repeating a gag about a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater; it is an animal that jumps, also Kanga and Roo of the Pooh books.
explanation.definitionFit: The kangaroo moves by hopping on its hind legs, so it is a natural jumper.

clue.text: Women united in voice backing a certain 22?

indicators.note: going backwards, the letters are read from the end
the united letter goes in the voice

parts.note: alto is a singing voice

explanation.surface: Women united in voice give support to a particular songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 is ROBIN, and the certain one is Robin Hood, the legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood was a famous outlaw, so this is what one particular Robin was.

clue.text: Flier one resents apprehending on sight

indicators.note: the outer word apprehends, seizes and holds, the inner letters

parts.note: a hater is one who resents
taken as written
the eye is the organ of sight

explanation.surface: A pilot with a grudge arrests someone on sight.
explanation.walkthrough: Honey also nods to Pooh's favourite food.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeyeater is an Australasian bird, and a flier is anything that flies, especially a bird.

clue.text: President hardly needing to get involved with CIA

indicators.note: the letters get involved, tangled together, with the agency's letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the US intelligence agency's initials

explanation.surface: A president barely needs to tangle with the CIA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President' suggests a head of state, but it means one who presides over a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who chairs a meeting presides over it, so she is its president.
